reason: 'With a (whitish) bloom' is the waxy surface bloom that PATO glaucous defines, as in the earlier rule for pruinose (C222).
Mixes two meanings: French 'soudé' (fused, i.e. connate/adnate) and 'with sutures' (a part, rejected as a generic part before). No single quality fits.
A count of one seed (suffix 'seeded' -> seed in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv), like few-flowered; the bearer of 'single-seeded nutlets' is the fruit.
glaucous (PATO_0104277) with value_qualifier 'sub' and the whole word as cue, as for suborbicular.
'Parenchymatous' = made of parenchyma; PO lists 'portion of parenchymatous tissue' as a synonym of parenchyma. Cell bearers ('exothecial cells parenchymatous') fit poorly and may stay unresolved.

The negation of ligulate, which rule C189 maps to strap-shaped (corollas, petals, sepals). For leaves and stipules 'not ligulate' may instead mean ligule (PO_0020105) absent and should be checked in context.
A cross-shaped lip or fruit cross-section is shaped like a cross, which is PATO x-shaped. 'Disposées en croix' is an arrangement (opposite pairs at right angles) and stays outside this rule.
Opening along the septa is FLOPO septicidal, which is already a kind of dehiscent. 'Septicidally then loculicidally' is a sequence of two values.
Heterophylly means the leaves of one plant occur in distinct forms, which is FLOPO dimorphic stated of the leaves. When the bearer is the whole plant, it should be replaced by the leaf (PO_0025034).
Negation of FLOPO gibbous, the same form as unlobed. 'At base' goes in the part-of-bearer slot.
Cochleariform = spoon-shaped: a concave shape like the bowl of a spoon, which is PATO spoon-shaped (not spatulate, which is a flat outline).

target: new: two values of one bearer (ovate FLOPO:0991024 and elongated PATO_0001154)
reason: This is not a continuum between two shapes. The outline is ovate but drawn out, so both values hold, as in the 'obliquely ovate' decision.

Possibly subacute (FLOPO:0991096), an acute point blunted at the tip, but the reading is doubtful: floras use it for an apex between obtuse and acute, and examples like 'acute or emarginate' and 'acute to rounded' show no fixed meaning.
'With a callus' states a part. The botanical callus has no class (PO_0005052 plant callus is tissue-culture callus), and 'callus' was rejected as a generic part before.
A relation that needs the centre the rows or lines share, and it mixes the arrangement of parts (scales, tubercles in rows) with surface markings (seed, bark, wood).
Star-like corollas, coronas and fruit cross-sections radiate from a common centre, which is PATO star shaped (EXACT synonym stellate).

label: latrorse
definition: An orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's facing and opening towards the sides, neither towards nor away from the centre of the flower. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991164 introrse and FLOPO:0991165 extrorse.
reason: An anther term that completes the set introrse/extrorse; PATO lateral orientation is an anatomical direction, not a direction relative to the flower centre.
Gradually curving inward. FLOPO:0991145 inflexed is an abrupt bend, so the general PATO curved fits, as for arcuate (C185). The inward direction is lost unless an 'incurved' class is added later.
Bending spines, stamens, corolla throats have an angle in their length: PATO bent. The direction words (downward, upward, over) are separate statements.
Bowed = curved like a bow, the same as the rule for arcuate (C185).
Tongue-shaped = ligulate, which PATO strap-shaped names in its definition (as rule C189).
A count of one flower (suffix 'flowered' -> flower in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv), the same pattern as few-flowered.
Teeth, hairs and lobes pointing forward (towards the apex) are antrorse.
The first half of a phrase like 'few- to many-flowered', where the part noun is given only once; once rejoined it is the counted-part pattern with the vague number 'few', as for few-flowered.
A perigynium or achene narrowed into a stalk-like base is stipitate (borne on a stalk). 'Stipe-like internode' and the 'part:' fragment stay unresolved.
Three or more primary veins radiating from one point is PATO actinodromous. Counts such as 'palmately 5-9-nerved' also take the count-of-parts pattern.
A parabolic sinus is an open U. However, PATO U-shaped has the synonym horseshoe shaped, which the floras contrast with parabolic ('parabolic to hippocrepiform'), so the rule merges that distinction.

target: new: two values of one bearer (streaked FLOPO:0991206 and white PATO_0000323 of the streaks)
reason: Streaked is a FLOPO value, and white is the colour of the streaks: a compound of two values, not a new term.
Spikelets, glands and stems densely packed are close together; this is the opposite of FLOPO distant, i.e. PATO crowded. A whole compact inflorescence is condensed (C188).
A degree adverb cut off from its shape ('narrowly to broadly ovate', 'narrowly so'), so it is a fragment and no quality by itself.
